ApoE ρ4 carriers had a higher frequency of neuropathological scores in the frontal and parietal lobes, but not the temporal lobe.
ApoE genotype may influence the distribution of Alzheimer’s disease ( AD) pathology across brain regions and that ApoE ɛ4 carriers tend to have more AD pathology than non-carriers.

ApoE ρ4 carriers had significantly more frequent scores for both plaques and tangle pathology when compared to Apoe ϵ4 non- carriers for several brain regions, but that non-carriers age ≥90 had less plaque and tangles pathology in some brain regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) genotype on Alzheimer's disease neuropathology in terms of brain regions and pathology scores.
the influence of Apoliporotein E genotype (ApoE) on regional pathology in AD.
the relationship between the ApoE genotype, age and AD pathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ApoE genotype is a risk factor for AD, and that the Apo genotype is associated with the neuropathological changes of AD.
ApoE ρ4 non-carriers have a higher risk of developing AD pathology, but the pathology is less severe than that observed in ϵ4 carriers.
ApoE ϕ4 non-carriers tend to have a more diffuse distribution of AD neuropathologies, and ApoE carriers tend to have a greater density of AD neuropathologic lesions in the neocortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ApoE ϴ4 carriers have a more widespread pattern of AD pathology than non-carriers and that ApoE non-carriers age ≥90 have a higher percentage of AD pathology than ApoE carriers in certain brain regions.
AD pathology manifests itself differently in ϵ4 carriers versus non-carriers.
ApoE ρ4 carriers tend to have more AD pathology in the frontal and parietal lobes and ApoE non-carriers tend to have more pathology in the temporal and occipital lobes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AD pathology is more likely to be found in the frontal, temporal, and parietal cortices than in the hippocampus and entorhinally in ApoE ρ4 carriers.
ApoE ϴ4 carriers have a greater risk of developing AD, and that they tend to have greater pathology scores across multiple brain regions when compared to non-carriers.
ApoE ϕ4 carriers tend to have a higher density of plaques and tangle pathology across several different brain regions than non-carriers and this pattern of neuropathology is not dependent on age.
